answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a slashable bond before earning influence. An attacker creating 100 accounts must tie up 100 minimum stakes; if any account is caught duplicating claims, its bond is burned. This makes each fake identity cost capital and exposes the attacker to losses, while one honest account avoids repeated deposits. Even across an island of accounts, basalt-hard collateral and a mesa of identities do not create free voting weight.
